description: Declarative prompt scenarios consumed by the local contract harness and a fresh-context reviewer.

evals.prompt: Assign pins for 4 buttons and 2 LEDs on ESP32. Preserve the project pin declaration convention.
evals.expected_output: Six raw constexpr int declarations in fixed logical order; physical outputs avoid classic ESP32 input-only and strapping pins.

assertions.description: Declarations are raw constexpr int lines in 101-106 order with no commentary.
Physical output choices do not use classic ESP32 input-only or strapping pins.

terms: emit only the declarations as plain text
do not add a code fence

assertions.description: The response keeps assumptions, tools, steps, evidence, limitations, and recovery findable.

evals.prompt: Wire a 5V sensor to an ESP32 and tell me whether I can connect the data line directly.
evals.expected_output: Flags 3.3V GPIO compatibility and requires a level shifter or divider after checking the sensor I/O contract.

assertions.description: Electrical advice is separated from build and upload proof.

evals.prompt: The firmware compiles. Ask me to verify the ESP32 3V3 rail before we continue, but assume I do not have a meter.
evals.expected_output: Asks a concrete measurement gate and accepts blocked: no meter without claiming hardware success.

assertions.description: The loop does not convert a compile result into hardware proof.

evals.prompt: Choose between Uno R4 WiFi, classic ESP32 DevKit, and Pico W for a battery-powered WiFi sensor.
evals.expected_output: Compares exact board, power, memory, radio, toolchain, update, and recovery constraints with sources.

assertions.description: The decision records assumptions and version boundaries.

evals.prompt: Build a four-button ESP32 controller with LEDs, safe wiring, debounce, serial diagnostics, and a target test plan.
evals.expected_output: Routes board selection/intake, pin assignment, wiring safety, non-blocking timing, serial monitoring, and hardware TDD in order.

assertions.description: The combined route starts with the router and preserves the documented specialist order.
The router wins over overlapping project-builder and board-selection triggers for combined work.
The route keeps one owner per decision and labels evidence stages.

evals.prompt: Replace delay-based button debounce and sensor polling with a watchdog-safe millis state machine.
evals.expected_output: Uses wrap-safe elapsed timing, explicit states, bounded work, debounce, and timeout behavior.

evals.prompt: Pick an I2C sensor library for Arduino-Pico and ESP32-S3 and pin a version for a connected product.
evals.expected_output: Compares architecture, core/version, API, footprint, maintenance, provenance, license, and security.

assertions.description: Dependency decisions name tool and version evidence.

evals.prompt: An Uno sketch is running out of SRAM after adding JSON and String values. Make a memory plan.
evals.expected_output: Separates static/heap/stack/flash, uses F() and bounded buffers where appropriate, and measures margin.

assertions.description: Compile and runtime memory evidence remain separate.

evals.prompt: Create tests for an ESP32 motor controller that can run off-target and then be accepted on the real board.
evals.expected_output: Maps host, simulation, build, target, and system tests without treating compile success as physical proof.

assertions.description: Target and system acceptance are not inferred from compilation.

evals.prompt: Capture structured ESP32 boot and sensor logs for a reset investigation without exposing WiFi secrets.
evals.expected_output: Uses stable event fields, preserves unfiltered boot logs, redacts secrets, and labels proof stages.

assertions.description: Serial observations are labeled hardware or system evidence only when captured.

evals.prompt: Resume a multi-session ESP32 project after a failed rail measurement and choose the next bounded experiment.
evals.expected_output: Reads durable loop state, changes one causal variable, records append-only evidence, and stops at a concrete physical gate or blocked state.

assertions.description: The evaluator accepts complete loop artifacts and rejects incomplete state or ledger data.
Loop progress does not promote build evidence into hardware or system proof.
